FRENCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #16
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: FRENCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.

2. When practising Listening for Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.

3. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

4. The French word for “book” is: (1 mark)
   A. chaise
   B. porte
   C. fenêtre
   D. livre

5. “Bonjour” is used to say: (1 mark)
   A. Good night only
   B. Thank you
   C. Good morning / hello
   D. Excuse me

6. When practising Listening for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Comprehension.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Comprehension.

7. When practising Reading for Comprehension, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Comprehension.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Comprehension.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Comprehension.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

8. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

9. When practising Grammar, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Grammar.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar.

10. When practising Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing.

11. When practising Oral expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Oral expression.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Oral expression.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Oral expression.

12. When practising Persuasive speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Persuasive speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Persuasive speaking.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Persuasive speaking.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Oral expression and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Listening for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Vocabulary.

3. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.

4. D — livre

5. C — Good morning / hello

6. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Comprehension.

7. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Comprehension.

8. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

9. A — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar.

10. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing.

11. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral expression.

12. C — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Persuasive speaking.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Vocabulary; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Grammar; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Oral expression; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Listening for Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
